rationale: The csharp lane's three surviving R1 (no regex) sites. The plan's R1 row says the honest test of the analyzer's `no AST path` claim is to PROBE the grammar, and both probes said the claim was false: an `operator_declaration` carries the operator token as an anonymous child with the FIELD `operator` (`checked` is a separate anonymous sibling) and a `conversion_operator_declaration` carries the target in the FIELD `type`; a using directive carries the alias in the FIELD `name` with the target as the first named child after the anonymous `=`. Each regex was ALSO wrong in a way text cannot repair. (1) `/using\s+([\w.]+)\s*=/` cannot tell alias from target — in `using A = B.C;` and `using A = Plain;` the two positions hold the same shape — and MEASURED (`script/m14/tmp/cs-using-alias-probe.ts`) `using Alias = Plain;` published `module: "Alias"`: the alias as the module, with the real target `Plain` named nowhere in the payload, so the dependency edge pointed at a name no namespace is imported from. Now `module: "Plain"` with `usingAlias: "Alias"`, and this fixture forbids a references edge to either alias spelling. (2) `/\boperator\s+(checked\s+)?([^\s(]+)/` stops at the first `(`, so a conversion target written with a space before the parenthesis was TRUNCATED (`implicit C` for `implicit operator C<T>(...)`) — pinned here by the Spaced class, whose name is the canonical `implicit Box<Plain>`, with the truncated and the spacing-carrying spellings both forbidden. The controls are load-bearing: a plain `using Json;` and `using System.Text;` must not be read as alias forms, and every ordinary operator keeps its exact pre-R1 spelling (`operator +`, `operator checked +`, `operator ==`, `implicit int`), because the whole lane's expectations name these symbols.

expectImports.comment: plain dotted control: no alias form
plain single-identifier control — must NOT be read as an alias directive
`using Alias = Plain;` — the TARGET, not the alias (pre-R1 this published "Alias")
`using static System.Math;` — the static form is a plain directive in this grammar

expectRelationships.note: the alias is published as metadata and the TARGET as the module/dependency — the two roles are distinguishable now
plain single-identifier using: no alias metadata may appear on it
a checked operator is a distinct member from its unchecked twin
the IDENTITY COLLISION pin: `implicit operator int` and `explicit operator int` are two members of ONE type, and both published as the same name (`operator int`) while the conversion pattern was dead
the twin that used to collide with it

forbidRelationships.note: the pre-R1 fabrication: the ALIAS published as the imported module name
the same class on the qualified form
